text_visible: The "rust" does not affect the jet's structure or operations.

It is not structural corrosion. The airframe is aluminum, titanium, and carbon composites — none of which rust. The brown streaks are surface oxidation of iron ferrite particles in the outermost radar-absorbent material (RAM) coating, caused by salt air, humidity, jet blast, and carrier conditions.
Official assessments from the F-35 Joint Program Office and Lockheed Martin confirm the discoloration stays limited to the coating surface and does not compromise integrity or performance.

Pre-service testing showed radar signature remained essentially unchanged after heavy simulated wear. A revised top-coat formula now prevents the discoloration on new jets and is applied to existing ones during maintenance.
